records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — Host deletion has no rejection handler, leaving failed deletes as silent unhandled promise rejections with no actionable feedback.
records.rationale: In embeddable-host.js.es6 the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, unlike the save action which explicitly uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. A failed destroy (e.g., server error, 403/500) would leave the promise rejected with no user feedback and the row still present, an inconsistency with the pattern established in the same new file. This is a substantive, code-grounded review concern rather than a verifiable runtime defect in the diff itself.
records.stripped_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — Host deletion has no rejection handler, leaving failed deletes as silent unhandled promise rejections with no actionable feedback.

This is a performance/scalability risk on a hot public path, not a correctness defect, making it important_non_bug.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Migration dereferences the first embed_category row even when no override exists, so default installations can fail before deployment completes.
records.rationale: The migration runs `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` unconditionally. On a default installation where no 'embed_category' site_settings row exists, the query returns an empty result set and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and failing the migration. The guard `if category_id == 0` only covers a value of 0, not a missing row.

WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` — the fallback `if category_id == 0` runs only after dereferencing `[0]`, so if the embed_category setting row is absent (never overridden), the query returns an empty array and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError before the uncategorized fallback is reached. records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migrated hosts are inserted without the model's normalization, so existing URL-form entries such as https://example.com silently stop matching after upgrade.
records.rationale: The migration inserts migrated site_setting values verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without applying the model's before_validation normalization (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and path stripping). Meanwhile, lookup uses `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` in `record_for_host`, so a migrated entry like 'http://example.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' (values explicitly shown in specs as valid old inputs) would never match requests after upgrade, silently breaking embedding for those hosts. Confirmed from diff lines.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Destructive setting deletion is embedded in a change migration with no reversible down path, so rollback cannot restore the prior configuration.
records.rationale: The migration uses `def change` while running `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` (and SQL INSERTs), which Rails cannot reverse — rolling back would drop the new table but the deleted settings and their values are unrecoverable. This is a concrete, diff-grounded migration completeness/irreversibility concern, not a runtime defect.
